title: Trusted Recovery Ingress POST raw-body binding

phases.objective: Bind signed Staging Recovery POST ingress to the exact raw body bytes while preserving GET empty-body semantics, durable replay protection, host isolation, and zero provider or Production mutation.

e2e_journeys.actor: Activation Gateway and Staging Recovery origin
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Send signed Recovery GET and POST requests through the canonical Activation Gateway Worker into the Staging Recovery origin verifier.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Allowed GETs remain body-empty, allowed POSTs are accepted only when method, exact path, request id, auth digest, policy identity, raw-body digest and durable replay claim all match.
steps: Capture exact raw JSON bytes for POST /admin/recovery/staging/* before Express JSON parsing.
Bound the Worker request body once and sign the SHA-256 of those same bytes before forwarding them upstream.
Resolve the explicit GET/POST allowlist for each Recovery path and reject methods or paths outside that matrix.
Recompute the SHA-256 digest from req.rawBody at the origin and compare it with the signed body_digest.
Reject changed-body substitution, GET-to-POST signature reuse, wrong-path reuse, replay, and a nonempty POST signed as an empty body.
Preserve durable atomic replay claim, trusted host identity, Staging-only authority and direct-origin fail-closed isolation.
assertions: GET contract/readiness/certification remain empty-body signed requests.
POST rollout-plan, dark-deploy-dry-run and bounded internal authority paths require captured raw-body bytes.
JSON.stringify(req.body) is never used as verification input; verification hashes exact raw bytes.
The Worker hashes the same bounded bytes forwarded upstream.
A valid signed POST reaches the Recovery route; changed body, changed method, changed path and replay are rejected before route execution.
Direct-origin and wrong-host requests remain unavailable.
No provider mutation, database mutation, migration apply or Production mutation is introduced.
Live Staging certification remains required before any rollout.
